synopsis: Toyota’s SEnS+ (August 2021) uses a rear stereo camera to distinguish people from objects and slows the forklift by cutting power, rather than using the brake to decelerate and automatically stop [f15785, f1407, f15786]. This distinction limits its relevance as a precedent for automatic braking: the reported intervention is power reduction, not brake-based stopping [f1407, f15786]. In the on-road regulatory context, Toyota joined the Alliance for Automotive Innovation and Volkswagen in petitioning for reconsideration of FMVSS 127, raising false-positive risk among other concerns [f1517]. Separately, the planning chapter cites Toyota cases and modelling as evidence supporting set-based design and parallel paths, although the supplied fact does not specify those cases or modelling results [f10087].

relations.note: Both state SEnS+ does not use brakes to decelerate and automatically stop.
Glossary adds the August 2021 date and rear stereo-camera detection to power-cut deceleration.
Power-cut slowing specifies the alternative to brake-based deceleration and automatic stopping.
